notes: Read by scripts/check-deps.mjs and by the quarterly pass in .claude/skills/polaris-tech-lifecycle/references/dependency-audit.md. NEVER read by anything under src/ at runtime: npm majors publish no end-of-life dates, and which major an install runs is fixed by its build, so this is a repo fact rather than a per-install monitoring signal. targetMajor is the major this repo intends to be on; check-deps fails when the installed major is below it.

npm.name: undici
npm.note: Moved 6 -> 8 on 2026-09-09 and the move was NOT trivial, contrary to what this note used to claim: it broke FortiManager and standalone FortiGate for every integration with verifySsl:false (connection test, discovery, DHCP/quarantine push, response-time probes). undici 8 rewrote the dispatcher handler interface (onRequestStart/onResponseStart replaced onConnect/onHeaders), and the Agent built here was being handed to Node's GLOBAL fetch, which is served by the undici bundled into Node (process.versions.undici — 7.24.4 on Node 24.14.1), not by this dependency. The v8 Agent rejects the v7 handler: TypeError 'fetch failed', cause UND_ERR_INVALID_ARG 'invalid onRequestStart method'. Nothing caught it — typecheck, npm audit and the whole suite were green, because the Agent was only ever paired with a STUBBED global fetch in tests. Fixed 2026-09-10: src/utils/tlsDispatcher.ts exports tlsFetch, which takes BOTH the fetch and the Agent from this dependency, since a dispatcher is only valid to the undici copy that created it. Surface: tlsFetch, the Agent, and the Dispatcher/RequestInit/Response types. NEVER pair insecureTlsDispatcher() with globalThis.fetch again — that reintroduces the skew silently. tests/unit/tlsDispatcher.test.ts now dispatches over a real local server, so the next mismatch fails a test instead of a device.

go.name: github.com/shirou/gopsutil/v3
go.note: Reads OS internals for the sample streams - a bump can change what a metric means on one platform and not another. Verify one Linux and one Windows agent before shipping.

go.name: golang.org/x/sys
go.note: The syscall layer under gopsutil. Its go directive tracks the current Go release closely — v0.44.0 (the first with the AIKIDO-2026-11041 fix) already requires go 1.25, and v0.48.0 requires 1.26 — so this module cannot be bumped independently of the Go floor. Cross-compile all six targets after a bump; a syscall package can build on one GOOS and fail on another.
